problem.description: PR #1084 correctly recycles previously task-capable workers whose completed cycle is stale, but a newly spawned self-heal worker may still be alive inside synchronous pre-cycle local source refresh/rendezvous/resident-request dispatch. Because the first task-capable tick is required within 3 seconds while resident dispatch may run much longer, treating that live startup PID as stale can terminate healthy in-progress recovery before the first WorkerCoordinator cycle.
evidence: scripts/run_worker_runtime.py:index-0 maintenance and resident dispatch occur before runtime.cycle

planned_change: preserve PR #1084 recycling for a previously proven worker that later becomes stale/non-task-capable
mark a newly spawned alive worker whose first tick times out as pending-first-tick instead of terminating it
persist the startup baseline tick and exact PID
on later supervision, retain the same pending PID until its tick advances beyond baseline; then require normal freshness before reporting presence
never promote PID existence to runtime presence and never spawn a duplicate WorkerCoordinator

readme_impact.reason: Changes resident self-heal startup and failure-recovery semantics by distinguishing an in-progress first-cycle worker from a previously healthy stale worker.
